source: Adapted from Maredj et al. (2024) example + CK-12 Foundation, CC-BY-NC
notes: Pilot document. Structure directly based on the worked example in Maredj et al. [2024]. Used to calibrate the annotation guide and validator. 15 units, mixed media, 3 ECU blocks. | U010 is the main_unit of ECU02; it participates in relations via the ECU, not directly. This is correct ERG behaviour — the validator warning is a false positive for main_unit members of ECUs that are referenced only via their ECU container. | v2: Corrected structure. ECU03 and ECU04 are multinuclear co-nuclei of Course, giving them weight 3.0 = same as Course. This matches [2] Table 2.

units.label: Who is Pythagoras? (image portrait)
units.content_summary: Portrait image of Pythagoras with a brief historical caption identifying him as the Greek mathematician (570–495 BC) associated with the theorem

units.label: Statement of the Pythagorean Theorem (text)
units.content_summary: Formal statement: In a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c²

units.label: Geometric Interpretation (video)
units.content_summary: Short animation showing the three squares on the sides of a right triangle, visually demonstrating that the area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of areas of the other two squares

units.label: Proof of the Pythagorean Theorem (text)
units.content_summary: Step-by-step algebraic proof using rearrangement of four right triangles inside a square

units.label: Usage Condition: right angle required (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram showing a right triangle with the right angle marked, and a non-right triangle with a cross, illustrating that the theorem applies only to right triangles

units.label: Worked Example: find the hypotenuse (text)
units.content_summary: Worked numerical example: given legs a=3, b=4, find c. Solution: c = √(9+16) = √25 = 5. Shows complete calculation steps.

units.label: Exercise 1: right triangle diagram (image)
units.content_summary: Diagram of a right triangle with legs labeled 5 and 12, hypotenuse labeled c. Students must find c.

units.label: Solution to Exercise 1 (image)
units.content_summary: Same diagram with solution annotated: c = √(25+144) = √169 = 13

units.label: Exercise 2: right triangle with unknown leg (image)
units.content_summary: Right triangle with hypotenuse = 10 and one leg = 6, asking students to find the missing leg b

units.label: Solution 2a: algebraic steps (text)
units.content_summary: Algebraic solution: b² = 10² - 6² = 100 - 36 = 64, therefore b = 8. Step-by-step working shown.

units.label: Solution 2b: diagram with answer (text)
units.content_summary: Annotated triangle diagram confirming b = 8 with all three sides labeled

units.label: The Course (main nucleus — root)
units.content_summary: Top-level course unit representing the complete lesson. In a real SCORM package this would be the course metadata/container. Duration represents navigation overhead.

units.label: Series of Exercises header (text)
units.content_summary: Section header: 'Practice Exercises — Apply the Pythagorean Theorem'. Introduces the exercise block.
